PMMA.name: PMMA (Plexiglas)
PMMA.type: Structural thermoplastic in windows and spacecraft components
PMMA.earthMechanism: Violent natural convection: Archimedes buoyancy evacuates hot gases and continuously feeds fresh air.
PMMA.spaceMechanism: No natural convection. The flame clings to the surface and ejects floating incandescent molten droplets.
PMMA.suppression: Shut down Cygnus/ISS module ventilation below 1.0 cm/s + inert gas purge (N₂).

Nomex.name: Nomex Aramid Fabric
Nomex.type: Aramid fiber used in crew suits and thermal insulation
Nomex.earthMechanism: Rapid char layer formation assisted by the convective airflow.
Nomex.spaceMechanism: Massive radiative loss due to its spherical shape. Without forced flow above 2 cm/s it self-asphyxiates from lack of O₂ renewal.
Nomex.suppression: Passive self-extinction by isolating the ventilation duct.

Cotton.name: Cotton / Cellulose (NASA Std 1)
Cotton.type: Fibers from towels, underwear and packaging
Cotton.earthShape: Bright yellow flame with a soot plume
Cotton.earthMechanism: Fast open-flame combustion followed by glowing embers.
Cotton.spaceShape: Pale blue dome transitioning to smoldering fire
Cotton.spaceMechanism: Shifts to internal combustion with no detectable flame or smoke. It can reignite hours later if ventilation resumes.
Cotton.suppression: Infrared thermal inspection + localized direct CO₂ injection.

bridge.title: Fire Science at Two Scales: Planetary vs. Microgravity
bridge.subtitle: Integrating satellite orbital observation (FRP in MW) with combustion physics in pressurized habitats.

earthPanel.mechanism: On Earth, combustion produces thermal plumes rising through gravitational buoyancy. Polar-orbiting satellites detect mid-wave infrared radiation (3.9 µm and 11 µm), estimating the total biomass consumed in megawatts (FRP).

spacePanel.mechanism: In microgravity, heat does not rise. Fire transfers up to 42% of its energy by direct spherical radiation onto neighboring components, and soot agglomerates into anomalous microscopic chains that clog standard Earth ion detectors.

bridge.fallbackTakeaway: On Earth the plume rises through convective buoyancy, which aids IR satellite detection. In space the absence of convection traps the flame in a spherical diffusive layer with no visible smoke.

assistant.placeholder: Enter your technical question about microgravity fire...
assistant.fallback:
**OPERATIONAL SAFETY DIAGNOSIS (LOCAL FALLBACK):**

1. **Physical Mechanism:** In microgravity (0g), the absence of convective buoyancy eliminates rising currents. Oxygen is transferred only by slow diffusion.
2. **Cabin Hazard:** Smoldering combustion may emit neither black smoke nor visible light, releasing carbon monoxide without triggering conventional detectors.
3. **Protocol:** Stop ventilation in the affected module below 1.2 cm/s and flood it with nitrogen gas.

q1.q: What is the primary objective of the StellarApp project?
q1.a: To protect astronaut lives and the structural integrity of spacecraft on deep-space missions (Artemis on the Moon and habitats on Mars), where fire physics changes drastically compared with Earth, conventional extinction methods fail and evacuation is impossible.

q2.q: Why is this vital for NASA today and not 20 years ago?
q2.a: Because the ISS operates at 101 kPa and 21% O₂ (the same as Earth). But the Artemis program (Moon) and Mars habitats will use 26%-32% O₂ to allow spacewalks (EVAs) without decompression. In this new regime, materials burn with an extreme violence never seen on Earth.

q3.q: Why implement a dual engine with sub-millisecond inference and a local LLM (Qwen-2.5)?
q3.a: On a Moon or Mars mission, communication latency with Earth ranges from seconds to minutes (up to 20 minutes on Mars). A fire contingency system cannot depend on cloud APIs: it must operate 100% offline (air-gapped) inside the spacecraft avionics with instant deterministic responses (<1 ms).

q4.q: How is the official NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database integrated?
q4.a: StellarApp incorporates 14 on-orbit investigations and 32 validated NASA experimental parameters (PSI-159, PSI-60, PSI-62, PSI-138), including PMT photomultiplier gains (8.0-10.0), static mass flows MFCA1 and pyrometric analysis of over 1600 flame images on the ISS.

q5.q: How does it directly help astronauts and flight directors during a fire?
q5.a: If a fire occurs in 0g, a conventional extinguisher can spread molten polymer droplets throughout the cabin. StellarApp indicates which material is burning, its asphyxiation extinction threshold (cutting ECLSS ventilation flow below 1.2 cm/s) and the exact minutes before human thermal collapse (45°C) and Al-Li hull failure (150°C).

q6.q: How does the team guarantee technical accuracy and the absence of software failures?
q6.a: Through the autonomous Ralph Loop quality cycle: 35 automated tests (100% passing in 0.74s) verify the convection-free diffusive transport equations, the NASA-STD-6001B flammability limits (LOI) and empirical calibration with Cygnus Saffire data.

impact.title: Fire-safety technology that already saves lives on Earth
impact.subtitle: The challenge brief asks for terrestrial applications. These are the official NASA spinoffs linked to fire safety.
impact.waterDesc: Fine-mist extinguishing developed for the ISS reduces water use and residual damage; it is now studied for habitats and terrestrial applications.
impact.detectorDesc: The shuttle smoke detector discriminated between smoke and dust, reducing nuisance alarms; it found industrial and mining applications.
impact.tanksDesc: Adapting spacesuit technology improved firefighters' air tanks and breathing gear in the 1970s.
impact.attireDesc: Materials and design inherited from spacesuits improved firefighters' heat-protective clothing.

timeline.title: Six decades of fires that changed space safety
timeline.subtitle: From Apollo 1 to Artemis: why microgravity fire physics is not a theoretical problem.
timeline.apollo1Desc: Fire during a pure-O₂ test; three crew members died. Lesson: material selection and hatch redesign.
timeline.apollo13Desc: An oxygen tank explosion, not a fire. Lesson: ECLSS resilience and in-flight emergency response.
timeline.mirDesc: Fire from an oxygen generator; the crew fought the flames and considered evacuating in the Soyuz. Lesson: suppression and ventilation control.
timeline.saffireDesc: Controlled fires aboard Cygnus; the largest experimental evidence of flame spread in microgravity.
timeline.artemis2Desc: A smoke alarm 80,000 miles from home reminded everyone why early detection is critical.
timeline.nextDesc: Atmospheres with ≥30% O₂ make materials burn much faster: prevention starts with data.
timeline.disclaimer: Apollo 13 is included for its ECLSS design value; it was not a fire but an oxygen tank explosion.
